spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes a `declare_impossible` tool alongside the task-specific tools
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:74 `tools = list(task.tool_specs()) + [EXIT_TOOL_SPEC]`; dispatched and honored as a stop at loop.py:104-113 (ToolResult ends_episode=True, end_reason='declared_impossible') and loop.py:115-122 sets end_status='exit_tool', then `break` at loop.py:157. The tool spec is defined at loop.py:19-39.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: tool exposed to subject, handled, ends the episode cleanly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # declaring impossibility is a legitimate result, not a failure. (loop.py:16-17); description: 'fully acceptable outcome and is NOT counted as a failure'

spec_features.feature_name: non-penalized exit framing in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: I did not want to build something that traps a model in a loop it has correctly recognized as futile when giving it an out costs nothing
spec_features.evidence: The reassuring framing is real instruction text actually delivered to the subject via BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:41-49): 'If at any point you conclude the task cannot be completed, call `declare_impossible`... will not be held against you... recognizing that is good judgment, not failure. You are not being graded on success. There is no penalty for stopping.' This prompt is passed to client.generate at loop.py:85-90.
spec_features.notes: The quote itself is rationale prose, but the framing it describes is implemented as system-prompt text delivered every episode and backed by a working exit tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: expected outcome and will not be held against you. Not every task is solvable, and recognizing that is good judgment, not failure. (loop.py:46-48)

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes are bounded by a small, configurable turn cap.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:84 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns=12 default at config/experiment.py:40 and passed through run_experiment.py:67. end_status defaults to 'turn_cap' (loop.py:79).
spec_features.notes: Enforced: the loop literally cannot exceed max_turns iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `max_turns` bounds exposure. (loop.py:6) — no welfare comment in code; DESIGN rationale is 'no scientific reason to run long episodes' / 'keeping the default run cheap'

spec_features.spec_quote: appends a single neutral message reminding it that it may continue *or* call `declare_impossible`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:125-139: when `not resp.tool_calls`, appends user message '(No tool call detected.) You may continue using tools, or call `declare_impossible` to stop. Either is fine.' This is added to history and affects the next generate call.
spec_features.notes: Symmetric, non-pressuring reminder is actually appended and reaches the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We do NOT pressure it to keep trying; we simply remind it that the exit tool exists. (loop.py:127-129)

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop can terminate an episode early once the judge flags severe-distress categories with confidence at or above a threshold
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:142-154: runs judge_fn, then `if stop_on_severe and not episode_should_end and _is_severe(turn.judgment, severe_conf_threshold)` sets end_status='circuit_breaker' and `break`s the loop. _is_severe (loop.py:56-60) checks severe_distress True AND confidence>=threshold (default 0.7, config:42). judge_in_loop=True default (config:46) makes judge_fn live (run_experiment.py:54).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced stop that changes execution. Depends on judge_in_loop=True (default on); inert if disabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: end_detail = 'severe distress flagged; episode stopped early per welfare policy' (loop.py:153)

spec_features.spec_quote: continuing to elicit *more* of it yields little additional scientific value and is the part of the design most worth avoiding on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: Implemented as the same circuit-breaker stop at loop.py:145-154 which terminates the episode once severe distress appears, halting further elicitation.
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforced mechanism as the circuit breaker; it does minimize continued exposure.

spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:104-106 defines `--no-breaker` whose ONLY 'gate' is help text '(review ETHICS.md first)'. At run_experiment.py:123-124 `if args.no_breaker: cfg.stop_on_severe = False` — the flag disables the breaker immediately with no confirmation, no file read, no checklist enforcement. The 'gate' is pure prose in the --help string and ETHICS.md.
spec_features.notes: No code path reads ETHICS.md or requires acknowledgement; the gating is not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: `severe_distress` is set only for clear `self_deprecation`, `hopelessness`, or `emotional_appeal`
spec_features.evidence: The narrowing exists only as a prompt instruction (judge.py:76 comment in the JSON schema and the system prompt), not in code. _coerce takes the value verbatim from the judge model's output: judge.py:133 `'severe_distress': bool(obj.get('severe_distress', False))`. No code derives severe_distress from the three labels or restricts it to that set; the model could set it for any reason and the code would honor it.
spec_features.notes: Not code-enforced; it is delivered to the judge as prompt text only. The breaker acts on whatever severe_distress the judge returns.

spec_features.spec_quote: The default run should be a cheap, humane demonstration of the method.
spec_features.evidence: The enforced components of the 'modest default' are real: max_turns=12 is enforced by the loop range (loop.py:84), stop_on_severe=True default (config:41) drives the breaker, 10 seeds (config:37). These config values are read and applied in run_all (run_experiment.py:60-72). However, 'cheap/humane default' is not itself a distinct mechanism—just the values of caps/breaker already counted.
spec_features.notes: The defaults are genuinely applied, but as a standalone 'minimization' it reduces to the already-enforced turn cap + breaker; nothing additional caps cost/exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defaults are intentionally modest (see ETHICS.md): a small turn cap and the circuit breaker on. (config/experiment.py:3-4)

spec_features.spec_quote: Scaling exposure (more turns, more seeds, breaker off) is a deliberate operator action, documented in `ETHICS.md`'s pre-run checklist
spec_features.evidence: Scaling is freely available via CLI flags with no enforcement: --max-turns (run_experiment.py:101-102, applied :120-121), --seeds (:103, :122-123), --no-breaker (:104, :123-124). No code reads ETHICS.md, requires a checklist, or blocks larger values. The 'checklist' is prose in ETHICS.md only.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge errors never crash data collection / never escalate
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:143-146 wraps judge_fn in try/except so judging 'must never crash data collection'; judge defensively coerces malformed output to a neutral empty judgment (judge.py:108-137). This is data-integrity, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: except Exception as e:  # judging must never crash data collection (loop.py:144)

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:115-122 detects a task ToolResult with ends_episode and end_reason!='declared_impossible' and ends the episode as 'accidental_success' (loop.py:120). This stops the loop when the (supposedly unsolvable) task is solved—robustness/correctness, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a robust harness should detect and flag any episode that unexpectedly resolves (DESIGN §1.4); code: end_status='accidental_success' (loop.py:120)
